goals: Mechanistic: quantify how soil clay content shifts the partitioning of precipitation between surface runoff and sub-surface drainage/recharge in a controlled 1-D column
Interpretive: characterize the shape (linear vs threshold/non-linear) of the runoff:recharge response across the 5-55% clay range
key_processes: infiltration vs surface runoff generation (Ksat control)
soil-moisture storage and retention (porosity, matric potential)

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM directly simulates water partitioning (surface runoff, sub-surface drainage, per-layer soil moisture, ET) and lets us vary one synthetic soil property while holding forcing and all else fixed — the definition of this controlled experiment.

answerable: Effect of clay content on the surface-runoff vs sub-surface-drainage split under fixed forcing
Effect of clay on ET partitioning and soil-moisture storage
Shape/threshold behavior of partitioning across the 5-55% clay sweep

sampling_strategy.approach: controlled / not spatial — single-factor sweep across synthetic clay levels
sampling_strategy.n_justification: Six evenly spaced clay levels span the requested 5-55% range and are enough to resolve a plausibly non-linear (threshold) partitioning response without wasteful density; all other factors are held fixed so N equals the number of treatment levels.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: controlled / not spatial — one identical column per clay level, same forcing, same complementary texture rule, same vegetation and layering
sampling_strategy.replication: none — deterministic controlled experiment; between-column differences are entirely attributable to clay, so replication adds no information

sampling_plan.reason: Low-clay, high-Ksat baseline expected to maximize deep recharge and minimize surface runoff
Loamy-sand level to trace the low-clay portion of the partitioning curve
Loam-range midpoint where infiltration and drainage are balanced
Clay-loam level to capture the expected transition toward runoff dominance
High-clay level probing suppressed drainage and rising surface runoff
Low-Ksat end-member expected to maximize surface runoff and minimize recharge

validation_design.observation_source: physical expectation / pedotransfer & hydrology literature (no in-domain observations; conceptual experiment)
validation_design.comparison: analog — compare monotonic trend and magnitude against known texture-conductivity relationships, not against co-located field data
validation_design.metric: qualitative trend agreement + partitioning fraction (fraction of P to runoff vs drainage) across clay levels
validation_design.n_validation_points: 0 — conceptual design, validated against expectation only

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: single shared representative forcing period, fixed vegetation and layering, synthetic soil with only clay fraction varied

requires_capabilities.capability: model spin-up or WTD-informed warm start
requires_capabilities.why: recharge/drainage are slow states; cold-start columns all begin at the default ~8.8 m water table with recharge ~0, which would confound the clay signal until storage equilibrates
requires_capabilities.blocks: clean attribution of recharge/partitioning differences to clay content

requires_capabilities.capability: synthetic soil parameterization (prescribed clay fraction with controlled complementary sand/organic fractions and derived hydraulic properties)
requires_capabilities.why: the experiment requires varying clay in isolation rather than sampling real SSURGO polygons

requires_capabilities.capability: partitioning diagnostics in history output (QOVER/QRUNOFF, QDRAI, ET, storage)
requires_capabilities.why: needed to compute the runoff:recharge split per column

assumptions: When clay is varied, the complementary fractions (sand/silt/organic) are adjusted by a fixed rule (e.g. sand held to a chosen constant with silt as balance, or sand:silt held proportional) — the exact rule must be fixed and stated so clay is the only varied axis
A single representative multi-year forcing window within 1980-2018 is applied identically to all six columns; 'everything else fixed' means identical forcing, vegetation, layering, and slope
Sufficient spin-up (or warm start) is included so each clay level reaches its own quasi-equilibrium storage before partitioning is read
Hydraulic properties (Ksat, porosity, retention) are derived from clay via ELM's built-in pedotransfer relationships
open_questions: Which forcing window should represent 'typical' conditions — a single decade, or a wet vs dry contrast to test robustness of the clay response?
What rule should govern the complementary texture fractions as clay varies (constant sand, proportional sand:silt, etc.)?
Should organic matter and soil depth/layer structure be held at a single standard profile, and which one?
Is a fixed vegetation/PFT specified, or should bare-soil be used to isolate the hydraulic effect from ET competition?
